romaji: Suzuki-san wa, oyasumi no hi ni nani o suru koto ga suki desu ka?
english: Mr. Suzuki, what do you like to do on your days off?
exampleRomaji: Suzuki-san wa, oyasumi no hi ni nani o suru koto ga suki desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 鈴木(すずき)さんは、お休(やす)みの日(ひ)に何(なに)をすることが好(す)きですか？
exampleEn: Mr. Suzuki, what do you like to do on your days off?
audioPath: clips/001_鈴木さんは、お休みの日に何をすることが好きですか.wav
grammar2:
何(なに)をすることが好(す)きですか = what do you like to do
好(す)き (like) ↔ 嫌(きら)い (dislike)

romaji: Watashi wa ie de eiga o miru koto ga suki desu.
english: I like to watch movies at home.
exampleRomaji: Watashi wa ie de eiga o miru koto ga suki desu.
japaneseFurigana: 私(わたし)は家(いえ)で映画(えいが)を見(み)ることが好(す)きです。
exampleEn: I like to watch movies at home.
audioPath: clips/002_私は家で映画を見ることが好きです。.wav
grammar2:
映(えい)画(が) = movie
家(いえ) (home) ↔ 外(そと) (outside)

romaji: Tanaka-san wa dō desu ka?
english: How about you, Mr. Tanaka?
exampleRomaji: Tanaka-san wa dō desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 田中(たなか)さんはどうですか？
exampleEn: How about you, Mr. Tanaka?
audioPath: clips/003_田中さんはどうですか.wav
grammar2: どうですか = how about...

romaji: Watashi wa tomodachi to Kyōto e ryokō ni iku koto ga suki desu.
english: I like to travel to Kyoto with my friends.
exampleRomaji: Watashi wa tomodachi to Kyōto e ryokō ni iku koto ga suki desu.
japaneseFurigana: 私(わたし)は友達(ともだち)と京都(きょうと)へ旅行(りょこう)に行(い)くことが好(す)きです。
exampleEn: I like to travel to Kyoto with my friends.
audioPath: clips/004_私は友達と京都へ旅行に行くことが好きです。.wav
grammar2:
旅(りょ)行(こう)する = to travel
友(とも)達(だち) = friend

romaji: Kyōto wa omoshiroi desu.
english: Kyoto is interesting.
exampleRomaji: Kyōto wa omoshiroi desu.
japaneseFurigana: 京都(きょうと)は面白(おもしろ)いです。
exampleEn: Kyoto is interesting.
audioPath: clips/005_京都は面白いです。.wav
grammar2: 面(おも)白(しろ)い (interesting) ↔ つまらない (boring)

romaji: Kyōto desu ka.
english: Kyoto, you say?
exampleRomaji: Kyōto desu ka.
japaneseFurigana: 京都(きょうと)ですか。
exampleEn: Kyoto, you say?
audioPath: clips/006_京都ですか。.wav
grammar2: 〜ですか = ...right? / ...you say?

romaji: Ii desu ne.
english: That sounds nice.
exampleRomaji: Ii desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: いいですね。
exampleEn: That sounds nice.
audioPath: clips/007_いいですね。.wav
grammar2: いい (good) ↔ 悪(わる)い (bad)

romaji: Kyōto wa furui otera ga ōku arimasu ne.
english: Kyoto has many old temples, doesn't it?
exampleRomaji: Kyōto wa furui otera ga ōku arimasu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 京都(きょうと)は古(ふる)いお寺(てら)が多(おお)くありますね。
exampleEn: Kyoto has many old temples, doesn't it?
audioPath: clips/008_京都は古いお寺がたくさんありますね。.wav
grammar2:
古(ふる)い (old) ↔ 新(あたら)しい (new)
多(おお)く (many) ↔ 少(すく)ない (few)

romaji: Hai, Suzuki-san wa Kyōto e itta koto ga arimasu ka?
english: Yes, have you ever been to Kyoto, Mr. Suzuki?
exampleRomaji: Hai, Suzuki-san wa Kyōto e itta koto ga arimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: はい、鈴木(すずき)さんは京都(きょうと)へ行(い)ったことがありますか？
exampleEn: Yes, have you ever been to Kyoto, Mr. Suzuki?
audioPath: clips/009_はい、鈴木さんは京都へ行ったことがありますか.wav
grammar2: 〜たことがある = have done before

romaji: Iie, watashi wa ichido mo itta koto ga arimasen.
english: No, I have never been there even once.
exampleRomaji: Iie, watashi wa ichido mo itta koto ga arimasen.
japaneseFurigana: いいえ、私(わたし)は一(いち)度(ど)も行(い)ったことがありません。
exampleEn: No, I have never been there even once.
audioPath: clips/010_いいえ、私は一度も行ったことがありません。.wav
grammar2: 一(いち)度(ど)も〜ない = never once

romaji: Itsuka itte mitai desu.
english: I'd like to go there someday.
exampleRomaji: Itsuka itte mitai desu.
japaneseFurigana: いつか行(い)ってみたいです。
exampleEn: I'd like to go there someday.
audioPath: clips/011_いつか行ってみたいです。.wav
grammar2:
〜てみたい = want to try doing
いつか = someday

romaji: Jaa, kondo no yasumi ni ikimasen ka?
english: Well then, why don't we go during the next holiday?
exampleRomaji: Jaa, kondo no yasumi ni ikimasen ka?
japaneseFurigana: じゃあ、今度(こんど)の休(やす)みに行(い)きませんか？
exampleEn: Well then, why don't we go during the next holiday?
audioPath: clips/012_じゃあ、今度の休みに行きませんか.wav
grammar2:
〜ませんか = why don't we...?
今(こん)度(ど) = next time

romaji: Shinkansen de iku to sugu desu yo.
english: If you take the Shinkansen, you'll get there right away.
exampleRomaji: Shinkansen de iku to sugu desu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 新幹線(しんかんせん)で行(い)くとすぐですよ。
exampleEn: If you take the Shinkansen, you'll get there right away.
audioPath: clips/013_新幹線で行くとすぐですよ。.wav
grammar2:
〜と = if / when
すぐ = right away

romaji: Shinkansen desu ka?
english: The Shinkansen?
exampleRomaji: Shinkansen desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 新幹線(しんかんせん)ですか？
exampleEn: The Shinkansen?
audioPath: clips/014_新幹線ですか.wav
grammar2: 新(しん)幹(かん)線(せん) = Bullet Train (Shinkansen)

romaji: Toukyou kara Kyouto made nan jikan kakarimasu ka?
english: How many hours does it take from Tokyo to Kyoto?
exampleRomaji: Toukyou kara Kyouto made nan jikan kakarimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 東京(とうきょう)から京都(きょうと)まで何(なん)時(じ)間(かん)かかりますか？
exampleEn: How many hours does it take from Tokyo to Kyoto?
audioPath: clips/015_東京から京都まで何時間かかりますか.wav
grammar2:
〜から〜まで = from... to...
かかる = to take (time/money)

romaji: Ni jikan han kurai kakarimasu.
english: It takes about two and a half hours.
exampleRomaji: Ni jikan han kurai kakarimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 二(に)時(じ)間(かん)半(はん)くらいかかります。
exampleEn: It takes about two and a half hours.
audioPath: clips/016_2時間半くらいかかります。.wav
grammar2:
半(はん) = half
くらい = about

romaji: Totemo hayai desu yo.
english: It's very fast.
exampleRomaji: Totemo hayai desu yo.
japaneseFurigana: とても早(はや)いですよ。
exampleEn: It's very fast.
audioPath: clips/017_とても早いですよ。.wav
grammar2: 早(はや)い (fast) ↔ 遅(おそ)い (slow)

romaji: Ni jikan han desu ka, hayai desu ne.
english: Two and a half hours? That's fast, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Ni jikan han desu ka, hayai desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 二(に)時(じ)間(かん)半(はん)ですか、早(はや)いですね。
exampleEn: Two and a half hours? That's fast, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/018_2時間半ですか、早いですね。.wav
grammar2: 早(はや)い (fast) ↔ 遅(おそ)い (slow)

romaji: Demo, shinkansen wa sukoshi takai deshou.
english: But, the Shinkansen is a bit expensive, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Demo, shinkansen wa sukoshi takai deshou.
japaneseFurigana: でも、新幹線(しんかんせん)は少(すこ)し高(たか)いでしょう。
exampleEn: But, the Shinkansen is a bit expensive, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/019_でも、新幹線は少し高いでしょう。.wav
grammar2:
〜でしょう = right? (seeking agreement)
高(たか)い (expensive) ↔ 安(やす)い (cheap)

romaji: Ee, chotto takai desu ne.
english: Yes, it's a bit expensive, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Ee, chotto takai desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: ええ、ちょっと高(たか)いですね。
exampleEn: Yes, it's a bit expensive, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/020_ええ、ちょっと高いですね。.wav
grammar2:
ちょっと = a bit
ええ (yes) ↔ いいえ (no)

romaji: Demo, kousoku basu yori shinkansen no hou ga hayakute benri desu yo.
english: But, the Shinkansen is faster and more convenient than the express bus, you know.
exampleRomaji: Demo, kousoku basu yori shinkansen no hou ga hayakute benri desu yo.
japaneseFurigana: でも、高速(こうそく)バスより新幹線(しんかんせん)の方(ほう)が早(はや)くて便利(べんり)ですよ。
exampleEn: But, the Shinkansen is faster and more convenient than the express bus, you know.
audioPath: clips/021_でも、高速バスより新幹線の方が早くて便利ですよ。.wav
grammar2:
〜より〜の方(ほう)がいい = ...is more... than...
便(べん)利(り) (convenient) ↔ 不(ふ)便(べん) (inconvenient)

romaji: Sou desu ne.
english: That's right.
exampleRomaji: Sou desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: そうですね。
exampleEn: That's right.
audioPath: clips/022_そうですね。.wav
grammar2: そうですね = That's right.

romaji: Kyouto de wa doko ni tomaru tsumori desu ka?
english: Where do you plan to stay in Kyoto?
exampleRomaji: Kyouto de wa doko ni tomaru tsumori desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 京都(きょうと)ではどこに泊(と)まるつもりですか？
exampleEn: Where do you plan to stay in Kyoto?
audioPath: clips/023_京都ではどこに泊まるつもりですか.wav
grammar2:
〜つもりだ = plan to do
泊(と)まる = to stay (at a hotel, etc.)

romaji: Watashi wa itsumo furui ryokan ni tomarimasu.
english: I always stay at old Japanese inns.
exampleRomaji: Watashi wa itsumo furui ryokan ni tomarimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 私(わたし)はいつも古(ふる)い旅館(りょかん)に泊(と)まります。
exampleEn: I always stay at old Japanese inns.
audioPath: clips/024_私はいつも古い旅館に泊まります。.wav
grammar2:
旅(りょ)館(かん) = ryokan (traditional Japanese inn)
いつも = always

romaji: Ryokan no gohan wa totemo oishii desu yo.
english: The meals at the inn are very delicious, you know.
exampleRomaji: Ryokan no gohan wa totemo oishii desu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 旅館(りょかん)のご飯(はん)はとても美味(おい)しいですよ。
exampleEn: The meals at the inn are very delicious, you know.
audioPath: clips/025_旅館のご飯はとても美味しいですよ。.wav
grammar2:
美味(おい)しい (delicious) ↔ まずい (bad tasting)
ご飯(はん) = meal / rice

romaji: Ryokan desu ka, ii desu ne.
english: A Japanese inn? That sounds nice.
exampleRomaji: Ryokan desu ka, ii desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 旅館(りょかん)ですか、いいですね。
exampleEn: A Japanese inn? That sounds nice.
audioPath: clips/026_旅館ですか、いいですね。.wav
grammar2: 旅(りょ)館(かん) = ryokan (traditional Japanese inn)

romaji: Watashi wa Nihon no furui tatemono ga suki desu kara, kyoumi ga arimasu.
english: I like old Japanese buildings, so I'm interested.
exampleRomaji: Watashi wa Nihon no furui tatemono ga suki desu kara, kyoumi ga arimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 私(わたし)は日本(にほん)の古(ふる)い建物(たてもの)が好(す)きですから、興味(きょうみ)があります。
exampleEn: I like old Japanese buildings, so I'm interested.
audioPath: clips/027_私は日本の古い建物が好きですから興味があります。.wav
grammar2:
〜から = because
興(きょう)味(み)がある = to be interested in

romaji: Ryokan no chikaku ni kirei na niwa mo arimasu yo.
english: There are also beautiful gardens near the inn, you know.
exampleRomaji: Ryokan no chikaku ni kirei na niwa mo arimasu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 旅館(りょかん)の近(ちか)くにきれいな庭(にわ)もありますよ。
exampleEn: There are also beautiful gardens near the inn, you know.
audioPath: clips/028_旅館の近くにきれいな庭もありますよ。.wav
grammar2:
近(ちか)く (near) ↔ 遠(とお)く (far)
綺麗(きれい) (beautiful/clean) ↔ 汚(きたな)い (dirty)

romaji: Zehi mitai desu.
english: I'd love to see it.
exampleRomaji: Zehi mitai desu.
japaneseFurigana: ぜひ見(み)たいです。
exampleEn: I'd love to see it.
audioPath: clips/029_ぜひ見たいです。.wav
grammar2:
ぜひ = by all means / definitely
〜たい = want to do

romaji: Kyouto no aki wa momiji ga kirei da to itte imashita.
english: They said that the autumn leaves in Kyoto are beautiful.
exampleRomaji: Kyouto no aki wa momiji ga kirei da to itte imashita.
japaneseFurigana: 京都(きょうと)の秋(あき)は紅葉(もみじ)が綺麗(きれい)だと言っていました。
exampleEn: They said that the autumn leaves in Kyoto are beautiful.
audioPath: clips/030_京都の秋はもみじがきれいだと言っていました。.wav
grammar2:
〜と言(い)っていた = they said that...
紅葉(もみじ) = autumn leaves

romaji: Ee, totemo kirei desu.
english: Yes, it's very beautiful.
exampleRomaji: Ee, totemo kirei desu.
japaneseFurigana: ええ、とてもきれいです。
exampleEn: Yes, it's very beautiful.
audioPath: clips/031_ええ、とてもきれいです。.wav
grammar2: とても = very

romaji: Demo, aki wa hito ga ichiban ooi desu kara, yoyaku ga taihen desu.
english: But since autumn is the most crowded season, making reservations is tough.
exampleRomaji: Demo, aki wa hito ga ichiban ooi desu kara, yoyaku ga taihen desu.
japaneseFurigana: でも、秋(あき)は人(ひと)が一(いち)番(ばん)多(おお)いですから、予約(よやく)が大変(たいへん)です。
exampleEn: But since autumn is the most crowded season, making reservations is tough.
audioPath: clips/032_でも、秋は人が一番多いですから予約が大変です。.wav
grammar2:
一(いち)番(ばん) = the most
大(たい)変(へん) (tough/difficult) ↔ 楽(らく) (easy)

romaji: Sou desu ka.
english: I see.
exampleRomaji: Sou desu ka.
japaneseFurigana: そうですか。
exampleEn: I see.
audioPath: clips/033_そうですか。.wav
grammar2: そうですか = I see.

romaji: Jaa, hayame ni keikaku o tateta hou ga ii desu ne.
english: Then, it would be better to plan ahead, wouldn't it?
exampleRomaji: Jaa, hayame ni keikaku o tateta hou ga ii desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: じゃあ、早(はや)めに計画(けいかく)を立(た)てた方(ほう)がいいですね。
exampleEn: Then, it would be better to plan ahead, wouldn't it?
audioPath: clips/034_じゃあ、早めに計画を立てた方がいいですね。.wav
grammar2:
〜方(ほう)がいい = had better do...
計(けい)画(かく)を立(た)てる = to make a plan

romaji: Hai, sou shimashou.
english: Yes, let's do that.
exampleRomaji: Hai, sou shimashou.
japaneseFurigana: はい、そうしましょう。
exampleEn: Yes, let's do that.
audioPath: clips/035_はい、そうしましょう。.wav
grammar2: 〜ましょう = let's do

romaji: Ashita, watashi ga ryokan no jouhou o shirabemasu.
english: Tomorrow, I will look up information about the inn.
exampleRomaji: Ashita, watashi ga ryokan no jouhou o shirabemasu.
japaneseFurigana: 明日(あした)、私(わたし)が旅館(りょかん)の情報(じょうほう)を調(しら)べます。
exampleEn: Tomorrow, I will look up information about the inn.
audioPath: clips/036_明日、私が旅館の情報を調べます。.wav
grammar2:
調(しら)べる = to look up / check
明日(あした) = tomorrow

romaji: Yoroshiku onegaishimasu.
english: Thank you in advance.
exampleRomaji: Yoroshiku onegaishimasu.
japaneseFurigana: よろしくお願(ねが)いします。
exampleEn: Thank you in advance.
audioPath: clips/037_よろしくお願いします。.wav
grammar2: よろしくお願(ねが)いします = Thank you in advance.

romaji: Tanoshimi ni shiteimasu.
english: I'm looking forward to it.
exampleRomaji: Tanoshimi ni shiteimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 楽(たの)しみにしています。
exampleEn: I'm looking forward to it.
audioPath: clips/038_楽しみにしています。.wav
grammar2: 楽(たの)しみにする = to look forward to
